rule: Planner tool list, read from its '  - <name>' lines, is exactly ten named tools, and its frontmatter contains no Write, Edit or Bash
description: plugin/agents/cerebrate.md is the planner. Its frontmatter tools: list is what grants it tools, so this fixture pins that list. The set_check captures every line of the form '  - <name>' (two spaces, a dash, a space, then the name up to the first whitespace) and requires, in equal mode with expected_counts, exactly these ten tools, each once: Read, Glob, Grep, LSP, WebSearch, WebFetch and the four claude-mem search tools. An added tool fails as an extra, a duplicated tool fails its count, and a deleted tool fails as missing. A deleted list fails as ten missing tools. set_check is used because an added grant is the threat, and a presence pin can only notice deletion. The three frontmatter-absent consumers require that the substrings Write, Edit and Bash appear nowhere in the frontmatter, so a grant that contains one of them fails even when it is written outside the '  - <name>' form. A Bash(...) entry grants the whole Bash tool, so the Bash consumer is what keeps the planner without a shell. The source pin sits on the Do Not item that forbids writing, editing, creating, or deleting files; deleting that item is loud. What this fixture does not check: (a) what each listed tool can do; the pin claims names, never capability or meaning; (b) a tool written outside the '  - <name>' form, such as an inline list, a different indent or a second tools key, unless its text contains Write, Edit or Bash; no frontmatter parser backs this fixture, because tools/policy_check.sh keeps its frontmatter checks line-scoped: the frontmatter form is stable and a parser is a new failure surface; (c) body prose: absent is scoped to frontmatter, and the body is not read for grants; the extract regex is line-scoped and not limited to the frontmatter, so a body line in the '  - <name>' form would be captured and fail equal mode as an extra (the body has no such line); (d) grants from any other file, such as settings files, hooks, or the delegation that starts the planner; files is a literal list that names only cerebrate.md.

source.pattern: write, edit, create, or delete files
